title: How many tokens deep is alignment across model families? A comparative audit

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: determines whether shallow alignment is universal or training-recipe-dependent, directly informing which open-source models are safer to deploy and what training changes matter. Both outcomes (universal vs variable shallowness) are immediately actionable for practitioners.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: KL divergence computation between aligned and base model outputs is straightforward with HuggingFace. Reference code from Qi et al.'s GitHub repo is available. Loading multiple small models on Colab Pro requires some care but is well-documented. A beginner with mentor guidance can execute this.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: alignment depth curves for 4-5 model families using a fixed prompt set. Clear metric (token position at which KL drops below 10% of peak). The output is a comparison table and plot. Could fit within 30 hours if limited to 3-4 models.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al., 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep' (arXiv:2406.05946, ICLR 2025 Outstanding Paper) established the shallow alignment phenomenon and measured KL divergence between base and aligned models. Follow-up work includes 'Any-Depth Alignment' (arXiv:2510.18081) and 'Safety Alignment Depth: A Markov Chain Perspective' (arXiv:2502.00669). However, a systematic comparative audit across 4-5 model families (Llama, Gemma, Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek) using alignment depth curves with a standardized metric has not been the focus of a single paper—existing work tends to use 1-2 model families. The comparative angle adds value.
